transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Um, well, what finally made me schedule this appointment is that I just keep making these small but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll turn in applications or my research notes, and there will be errors... maybe a mislabeled artwork date or I'll just completely skip a question on a form. 

And the frustrating part is that I honestly thought I had checked everything over before handing it in. It's just happening enough that it's becoming a problem, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Do you find that you have been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years or longer?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself when I make those careless mistakes, but I don't feel sad or empty most of the time. My mood is generally pretty normal, honestly. It's really just the constant errors that are getting to me.
Do you often find it difficult to sit still or feel a need to move around when you are in situations where you are expected to stay seated?

No, not really. I don't have trouble sitting still. I can sit through a whole lecture or a long meeting without needing to get up or move around. It's more about keeping my focus while I'm sitting there, rather than needing to actually get up.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your day feeling anxious or worried about a wide range of different things, such as your work, your health, or your future?

No, not really. I don't think I'm an anxious person overall. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about my health or my future or anything like that. I get stressed when I realize I messed up on an application or an assignment, sure, but I definitely don't spend my day feeling constantly worried about a bunch of different things.
When you are working on tasks like your research notes or filling out forms, do you often find it difficult to maintain your attention until the task is finished?

Um, not really, no. I mean, if I'm working on something like research notes or a form, I can usually stick with it until it's done. It's not so much that I lose my attention and can't finish the task... I just end up making those careless errors I mentioned while I'm doing it. But getting through the actual task and finishing it isn't usually the problem.
Do you often find it challenging to organize your tasks, belongings, or schedule in a way that keeps things running smoothly?

Yeah, I definitely struggle with that. My apartment and my laptop are basically just a mess of half-started projects. I've got rent papers, gallery notes, article PDFs, and random to-do lists scattered everywhere. It's just really hard for me to figure out how to organize it all or even know what actually needs to happen first.
Looking back at your childhood, say during elementary school, did you struggle with these same kinds of organizational issues or careless mistakes back then?

Yeah, I actually did. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I had good ideas, but... I just always forgot to turn in my worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions for assignments. I missed a lot of little details back then, too. Honestly, the only way I got by was if my parents checked my backpack every single night to make sure I actually had everything. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a while.
In your day-to-day life, do you often find yourself forgetting things like appointments, errands, or where you put your keys or phone?

Yeah, definitely. I'll mean to do normal adult things, you know, like return an email, pay a bill, or pick up groceries... and then days later I realize I never actually did it. It just completely drops out of my mind.
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before a question has been completed, or do you find it difficult to wait your turn in conversations or group activities?

No, not really. I don't think I have a problem with that. I'm usually pretty good about waiting my turn to speak, and I don't really interrupt people or blurt things out. That hasn't really been an issue for me.
Do you often find that your mind feels like it's constantly 'on the go' or that you have an internal sense of restlessness, even if you are physically able to sit still?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't feel super restless inside or like I'm constantly on the go. My mind wanders a lot, obviously, but it's more like I just zone out or lose focus, not really that I feel driven like a motor or anything like that. I can sit still fine without feeling antsy.
